title: Mortgages
objective: After this level you can explain how a mortgage works and why it lasts for decades.
summary: A mortgage, a 'dead pledge', lets the lender take the property if it isn't repaid. Longer terms mean smaller payments but more total cost; early payments are mostly interest.

cards.headline: A mortgage is, word for word, a "dead pledge".
cards.body: The name comes from Old French. It's less grim than it sounds, and it explains exactly how a home loan works.

cards.headline: Why the pledge dies
cards.body: The pledge is the property. A mortgage gives the lender the right to take it if you don't repay the loan plus interest. So the pledge dies one of two ways: the debt is paid off and the lender's claim ends, or the payments stop and the borrower loses the home. Either way, the deal is over.

cards.headline: Why decades?
cards.body: Spreading a big loan over many years makes each payment smaller. Compared with a 15-year mortgage, a 30-year one usually has lower monthly payments, but a higher interest rate and a higher total cost. More years of borrowing means more years of paying Level 23's rent on the money.

cards.fact: Your first mortgage payments mostly pay interest.
cards.context: Early on, the balance is high, so most of each payment covers interest. As the balance shrinks, more goes to paying off the loan itself, until near the end most of it does. This is amortization, and it's why the share of the home you own grows much more slowly than the payments you've made.

mascot.line: Dead pledges and slow equity. Home loans come with surprisingly dramatic vocabulary.

cards.headline: Mortgages: explained
learned: The lender can take the property if payments stop
Longer terms: smaller payments, bigger total cost

questions.prompt: If a mortgage isn't repaid, what does the agreement let the lender do?

options.label: Take a share of the borrower's wages forever
options.rationale: The mortgage is pledged on the property.

options.label: Raise the price of the house
options.rationale: The lender doesn't set house prices.

options.label: Nothing: mortgages carry no pledge
options.rationale: The property is the pledge, hence "dead pledge".

questions.explanation: A mortgage gives the lender the right to take the property if the loan plus interest is not repaid.

questions.prompt: Why does most of an early mortgage payment go to interest?

options.label: The loan balance is still high
Banks add a penalty for new borrowers
options.rationale: No penalty: interest is simply charged on a high balance.

options.label: The interest rate starts high and then falls
options.rationale: The rate can stay fixed; the balance is what shrinks.

options.label: The first payments are held as a deposit
options.rationale: They're real payments, mostly covering interest.

questions.explanation: Interest is charged on the balance. Early on the balance is high, so most of each payment is interest: amortization.

questions.prompt: From Level 22: when a bank approves your mortgage, what happens to the amount of money in the economy?

options.label: Nothing: the bank passes on another saver's money
options.rationale: That's the textbook picture; lending creates a new deposit.

options.label: It shrinks, because the bank pays out cash
options.rationale: The bank credits a new deposit; money grows.

options.label: It grows: the loan creates a new deposit
It grows, because the house is turned into cash
options.rationale: The house is the pledge; the new money is the deposit.

questions.explanation: A new loan, a mortgage included, credits the borrower's account with a brand-new deposit: new money.
